edges.relationship: McKay's historical work is Gramscian by his own account: cultural hegemony in The Quest of the Folk (1994), and 'the Gramscian assumptions that have shaped my outlook' (2000)
edges.evidence_note: McKay's own words, read in full ("A Note on 'Region' in Writing the History of Atlantic Canada", Acadiensis 29:2, 2000, p. 89): 'the Gramscian assumptions that have shaped my outlook'. Muise (Acadiensis 27:2, 1998, read pp. 124, 128–132) reports that in The Quest of the Folk McKay places himself 'within a neo-marxist framework associated with the work of Antonio Gramsci' and quotes the book (p. 306): 'the concept of the Folk was and remains a powerful obstacle to the formation of a counter-hegemonic cultural politics'. Wright (Acadiensis 24:2, 1995, p. 132 n. 29): 'For a very skilled handling of Antonio Gramsci's theory of cultural hegemony by an historian see Ian McKay, The Quest of the Folk'. Critic: Palmer (2009) argues that McKay's Gramsci conflates hegemony and domination. The Quest of the Folk is given through these readers. Distinct from edge_844 (Gramsci → the liberal order framework, 2000): this arrow carries the influence on McKay's work from 1994, before the prospectus.

edge_844.relationship: The liberal order framework is Gramscian: liberal order as hegemony and the national-political 'commonsense' (2000)
edge_844.evidence_note: McKay's abstract (2000) maps Canada as 'a project of liberal rule in northern North America' through which 'liberal order became the national-political ‘commonsense’'. Ajzenstat (2009) describes McKay as recommending 'a Gramscian approach to Canadian history'; Pâquet (2009) names Gramsci, with Fernande Roy (1988), as one of the prospectus's two explicit influences; Palmer (2009) argues that McKay's reading of Gramscian hegemony is too seamless, conflating hegemony and domination. McKay's own Gramscian outlook is drawn separately (gramsci → ian_mckay, revision 1.149). PhD context: 9 of the 91 PhDs citing McKay 2000 also cite a Gramsci work.

rationale: The 1.129 McKay packet (data/extension-2026/canadian-person-links-2026-10-13/mckay/NOTES.md) recorded gramsci → ian_mckay as a lead and left it out because edge_844 carried Gramsci at entry level. The claims differ: edge_844 concerns the 2000 prospectus; the new edge concerns McKay's work from 1994, in his own words. No new sources: all four witnesses are existing records already read.
